claim: TheCreatorEconomy.com attributes a battery of statistics (62% burnout, 47% considered leaving in past six months, 71% workload increase, platform breakdown, financial-instability battery) to a 'Creator Economy Research Institute Q1 2026 study of 2,400 full-time creators' - but no organization by that name, no website, no report, and no independent citation of it exists anywhere on the web.
stance_target: reliability of the '2,400 full-time creators' attribution as a real, citable instrument
scope_conditions: AUDITED ABSENCE finding, recorded per run directive: targeted search for 'Creator Economy Research Institute' returns no hits besides this article itself. This claim documents that the cited instrument cannot be verified to exist, not a substantive burnout finding. Do not cite the 62%/47%/71% figures as sourced to a real n=2,400 study.
quoted_support: "Creator Economy Research Institute's Q1 2026 study of full-time creators revealed: 62% report experiencing burnout symptoms..." [no link, methodology, sampling frame, field dates, or country given anywhere in the article; independent search found no organization by this name]

claim: The article's headline 62% burnout figure and its 58%/depression framing closely mirror the independently-verified Creators4MentalHealth/Lupiani Insights study (n=542, North America, published November 2025) published roughly three months earlier, suggesting the '2,400 full-time creators' attribution may be a garbled or fabricated restatement of that real, smaller study rather than independent research.
stance_target: independence of the claimed 'Creator Economy Research Institute' figures from the real Creators4MentalHealth study
scope_conditions: Cross-source provenance comparison. The genuine C4MH study (source note in-sweeping-study-89-of-creators-claim-to-lack-access-to-specialized-mental-heal) reports 62% burnout among n=542 North American creators (published Nov 2025); this article's near-identical 62% figure attributed to an unverifiable n=2,400 'Q1 2026' instrument is the strongest evidence that the latter attribution is unreliable.
quoted_support: "The headline 62% is exactly the burnout figure published three months earlier by the Creators 4 Mental Health / Lupiani Insights study (n=542, North America, Nov 2025)" [note author's own cross-check, documented in the note summary]

claim: The article cites uncheckable named sources ('Dr. Sarah Chen' at Stanford studying creator mental health; creators '@sarahmakes' and 'Tom Henderson') and describes specific platform programs (YouTube 'Creator Wellness Program' launched January 2026, TikTok 'Creator Sabbaticals') as established fact with no citation or corroboration found elsewhere.
stance_target: reliability of named experts and platform-program claims in this article
scope_conditions: Documents a pattern of unverifiable named-source and program citations consistent with fabricated or unreliable content. Not evidence of any real burnout/attrition figure.
quoted_support: "'Offering six therapy sessions doesn't fix an algorithm that punishes people for taking weekends off,' argues Dr. Sarah Chen, who studies creator mental health at Stanford."
